views.title: 正视
views.prompt:
Create a camera-rotation view of the EXACT SAME miniature spherical planet and early gathering settlement in the reference image. This is a multi-view design study for one fixed game world, not another settlement or another development stage. Keep object identity, counts, ground layout, relative positions, coastline and materials consistent. Change ONLY the viewpoint requested below and reveal physically plausible previously hidden surfaces.

APPROVED ART: softly stylized semi-realistic 3D miniature diorama, natural clustered broadleaf woodland, fine grass and soil variation, gently weathered stone, simple crafted timber shelters, golden thatch roofs, warm natural daylight, soft shadows, restrained atmospheric depth, calm blue-green ocean with subtle ripple highlights, soft blue background. All important facilities should remain readable where they are visible. Keep the same time of day and world lighting. Landscape canvas 1536 x 1024, one complete spherical planet with a full circular silhouette, comfortable margins, almost orthographic camera. Terrain and facilities must wrap around a globe; buildings stand upright on their LOCAL spherical ground. Never flatten the world into an island, cutaway disk or rectangular scene.

FIXED INVENTORY AND TOPOLOGY, using directions as seen in the reference image:
1. ONE open timber CENTRAL STOCKPILE with a pitched brown roof and visible log, stone and sack piles is the settlement hub near the center of the developed region. Preserve its recognizable open front.
2. EXACTLY TWO modest thatch-roof dwellings are a compact group BEHIND the stockpile, towards the northern rocky ridge. Keep both at their original locations and sizes. Do not duplicate houses.
3. ONE open LOGGING LEAN-TO with timber piles sits at the edge of the dense upper-left woodland. It feeds the center by a short dirt path.
4. ONE open STONE QUARRY with stepped pale-gray rock cuts, squared stone blocks and small wooden working frames lies at the upper-right rocky hill foot. It is not a tunnel mine, smelter or masonry city.
5. ONE berry FORAGING PATCH with baskets lies left/front-left of the stockpile, between woodland and coastline. Preserve it as the food source.
6. ONE broad calm bay curves along the lower-left/front edge of the land. Preserve its recognizable concave coastline and prominent shore rocks. Water uses nuanced blue and teal tones, light reflections and gentle surface patterns. No waterfalls or elaborate surf.
7. The lower-right/front land is MOSTLY OPEN BUILDABLE GRASSLAND with sparse small plants and rocks, reserved for later growth. Do not fill it with new buildings or dense forest.
8. The existing narrow dirt paths connect housing and real workplaces to the stockpile. Preserve their ground footprints; they must rotate in perspective with the planet. A few tiny automatic workers may be present only at existing tasks.

There are NO farms, no granary, no workshop, no separate laboratory, no mining tunnel, no electric equipment, no cars, no army, no decorative monuments, no new islands and no extra settlements. Do not move occluded objects into view or duplicate them to make them visible. In side views, distant facilities can be naturally hidden by curvature, forest or the ridge. Unseen terrain continues conservatively as simple grass, woodland and water, with no new landmarks. Image contains no interface, text, letters, grid, arrows, title, labels or watermark.

CAMERA FOR THIS IMAGE:
FRONT ELEVATION from the settlement-front / open-stockpile-entrance side. Lower the camera substantially from the elevated reference viewpoint and look horizontally toward the planet center, approximately at globe-equator height. Keep the northern ridge pointing up. This must read as a straight FRONT view, not the original elevated three-quarter view: more vertical building fronts, less visible roof area, the bay occupies the lower/front globe and developed land rises behind it. Stockpile remains in front of the two houses, woodland appears on the left, rocky quarry on the right, with globe curvature and natural occlusion intact. The whole planet is visible and centered; never crop the lower ocean arc.
